esc-psychological-support-child-protecti.about:
Fundación Munasim Kullakita ( Instagram ) operates "Hogar Trampolín" in Bolivia, a specialized center providing comprehensive protection and rights restitution for girls and female adolescents who are survivors of human trafficking and sexual exploitation. The volunteer supports the lead psychologist in the emotional recovery and identity reconstruction of survivors aged 10-17. The mission focuses on three axes: - helping residents recognize themselves as victims to overcome guilt, - empowering them as survivors through resilience, and - fostering the ability to project a constructive future. Daily tasks include conducting psychological evaluations to guide staff interventions and providing individual and group therapeutic support tailored to cognitive development and cultural backgrounds. The volunteer assists in drafting monthly follow-up, monthly, and reintegration reports for legal authorities. A critical active component involves providing emotional containment during legal proceedings.

The programme is designed for young people who are interested in developing their own eco-social entrepreneurial ideas and concepts. It combines learning, reflection and practical experience. Participants will: explore topics such as intentional living, synergetic, sociocracy, collaborative decision-making, mindfulness, conflict management, shared responsibility and balancing individual and collective needs; explore how entrepreneurial activities can create value for themselves, their communities, other people and nature; work on their entrepreneurial ideas, develop concepts and prototypes, and receive support through peer learning, facilitated dialogues and direct exchange with other participants.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps team volunteering hosted by Thinkcamp Gem Eg in Küstriner Vorland, Germany; activity period 25 days (14 November 2026 – 8 December 2026). Topics: social inclusion and community work, environment and nature protection, health and wellbeing, education and non-formal learning, culture and creativity. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 37 other countries. Deadline: 2 November 2026.

Living and learning: Participants will stay together at Gut Herzershof, a remote learning and experimental location surrounded by nature, about 90 km east of Berlin. Community living is an important part of the project: participants will cook, eat, organise daily life and take responsibility for shared spaces together. The programme combines facilitated learning with practical work on participants’ entrepreneurial ideas, including discussions, workshops, creative activities and project work. Travel costs will be reimbursed according to ESC rules. The team will be supported throughout the programme by a facilitator. The learning process will follow a peer-to-peer approach, where participants learn from each other, exchange experiences and ideas, give feedback and support the development of each other’s entrepreneurial concepts. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.
